configuration.json.clientDriverCountScope: load phase only; count recorded after every worker connects; setup/validation excluded
configuration.json.workload: independent one-lot IOC buys, one pre-funded GTC maker, one trade per accepted command
configuration.json.loadModel: absolute fixed-arrival scheduler; bounded round-robin per-worker FIFO; one synchronous in-flight per worker
configuration.json.timeouts: A timeout is unknown. Worker retries the identical identity before advancing; original and resolved completion times remain distinct.

session-reap-after-setup.json.scope: session reclamation pause after closed clients; excluded from load and validation timing

load-result.json.latencyScope: Conditional on returned response; accepted-only distribution is separate. All offered accepted-command p99 is null if any arrival is dropped, rejected, errored or unresolved.
load-result.json.percentileMethod: nearest rank; all returned replies retained including responses after timeout/drain; not-sent and unresolved are counted separately, not given invented latency
limitations: Fixed finite window and bounded queues; queue-full is client admission loss, not server rejection
Each worker has one in-flight synchronous client; this measures this deployed client+cluster path, not an unconstrained engine limit
No synchronized-clock one-way latency and no production capacity SLA
Execute-start is an API timestamp, not first wire offer; scheduler delay and FIFO delay are included in end-to-end latency
Backlog counters are observational non-atomic snapshots, not exact queue conservation at an instant
Pause gateway/projector writers and use isolated trial state; shared-member load generation must be disclosed

session-reap-before-validation.json.scope: session reclamation pause after closed clients; excluded from load and validation timing

validation-start.json.scope: connect, snapshot read, replay and final checks; excluded from measurement

validation-timing.json.scope: connect, snapshot read, deterministic replay and final checks; excluded from load measurement
